summary.text: 不 is a common negative word meaning “not,” attested in oracle-bone inscriptions. Its original pictured subject remains disputed.

formation.text: 不 is treated as a whole pictograph, but what it depicts is unresolved: proposals include plant roots or a germ, a flower calyx, and a later dictionary explanation of a bird flying upward toward the sky. No separate phonetic component is supported.

components.text: Read 不 as one whole picture, not as established separate parts. Interpretations include roots or a germ, a calyx, and a later account of a bird rising toward a line for the sky; none is settled.

history.text: Oracle-style and seal-style forms are represented by modern redrawings. They illustrate different script traditions but do not establish the graph’s original subject or a sequence of graphic changes. The seal-style form reflects the transmitted dictionary tradition and its bird explanation.

uncertainties.text: The original referent is unresolved. A proposal holds that the graph was borrowed for negation because the pictured subject’s old name sounded like “not,” but neither that name nor the sound match is established. Negative use is broadly assigned to oracle-bone inscriptions of the 14th–11th centuries BCE, without a specific occurrence date.
No independent phonetic component or component-to-character sound comparison is supported. Reconstructions of the negative word do not establish how any proposed pictured subject was pronounced.

senses.text: 不 is attested as a negative particle in oracle-bone inscriptions. The corpus is dated broadly; no specific occurrence is dated here.

senses.period: Later Archaic Chinese; examples cited from the Analects and Xunzi
senses.text: 不 is used as a general verbal negative in later Archaic Chinese. The intervening development from its earlier particle use is not traced in detail.

senses.period: Modern Chinese; usage varies by language and dialect
senses.text: 不 commonly expresses negation, including as a negative prefix; its distribution varies across modern varieties.

developments.text: Early particle use and later general verbal negation are both documented, but the intervening development is not traced in detail.
Modern negation is documented, but a continuous chronology from Archaic usage to modern distributions is not established.

limitations.text: No earliest attestation of a literal root, germ, calyx, or bird meaning, or a dated path from any proposed picture to negation, is established.
Early negative use is assigned broadly to the oracle-bone corpus; a particular inscription date and a full chronology of later uses are unavailable.

items.period: Shang period style; modern drawing based on cited historical character references, without a specific artifact/date identified in the page description
items.caption: This oracle-script-style form of 不 has a tall central stroke and two sweeping sides. 不 is reported as a negative particle in oracle-bone inscriptions, though its original referent remains disputed.
items.alt: A black oracle-script-style glyph with a tall central stroke and two curved strokes descending to either side.
items.selection_reason: The visible form is legible as an oracle-style rendering of 不 and illustrates the early script tradition associated with its reported use as a negative particle. The plant-root, flower-calyx, and bird explanations remain competing interpretations.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern drawing, not a dated ancient artifact image
items.tradition: Seal script as transmitted in the Shuowen tradition
items.caption: This Shuowen seal-script-style form of 不 has a horizontal top and several descending strokes. Shuowen's bird-flying-upward explanation is a historical interpretation, not proof of the graph's original referent.
items.alt: A black seal-script-style glyph with a horizontal top and several strokes descending below it.
items.selection_reason: Its visible seal-style form gives a useful comparison with the oracle-style rendering. It also helps distinguish the transmitted Shuowen explanation from the unresolved debate over the graph's origin.

limitations.text: Both images are modern redrawings in historical script styles, not photographs or facsimiles of ancient inscriptions. Their appearance does not establish the graph's original referent or a sequence of graphic changes.

The graph's original referent remains unresolved: sources discuss root or germ, flower calyx, and Shuowen's bird account. Early use as a negative particle is reported, but a specific inscription date and a demonstrated path from the proposed referent to negation are not established.
